description: Shrubs or sub-shrubs. Stems climbing, internodes elongate, sometimes erect. Leaves opposite, usually ternately or pinnately compound, sometimes simple. Inflorescences definite. Stamens numerous, hairy or glabrous. Carpels uniovular, ovule pendulous. Achenes several to many, aggregated in a fruit, beaks usually elongated into a tail.</br></br>About 300 species in all continents. Ten species in Thailand.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Clematis  . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 49. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Evergreen climber, drying brownish or blackish. Stems glabrous, internodes with many striae. Leaves ternate, middle leaflets ovate to ovate-elliptic, 6.2–15.5 by 3.2–9 cm, truncate to cordate at base, acuminate to acute at apex, entire, chartaceous, main veins 5–7, inner veins branching above the outer, glabrous on both sides, prominently reticulate especially beneath, petiolules 1.8–4 cm long, lateral leaflets similar to the middle ones, shortly petiolulate, petioles 3.5–11 cm long, glabrous, dilated near base. Inflorescences terminal and axillary, thyrsiform or subpaniculate, 9–80-flowered, pubescent in upper part with crisp white hairs, peduncles 3–8 cm long, subvillose, bracts linear, pedicels 1–3.5 cm long, subvillose, bracteoles linear, minute. Flowers flat, 2–2.5 cm diam. Sepals 4, oblong, obtuse at apex, 10–13 by 3–4 mm, creamy white to yellowish green, drying brownish, upper surface glabrous, lower surface pubescent with crisp, white hairs, especially along margins. Anthers oblong, lateral, 1.2–1.8 mm long, connectives hardly projected, filaments drying blackish to brownish, 6–8 mm long, filiform, glabrous, thinner than anther. Achenes drying blackish to brownish, elliptic, 7–10 by 3.5–4.5 mm, compressed, thick-margined, suddenly contracted to short stipe downwards, tapering to tail upwards, pubescent with appressed, dirty yellowish, 3–3.5 mm long hairs, tails 3.2–4 cm long, plumose with ascending, yellowish, long hairs, but shorter and appressed towards base.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Clematis burmanica . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 56. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Evergreen, often deciduous climber, robust, sometimes to more than 6 m tall, 1 cm thick, drying yellowish brown. Stems glabrous, internodes striate with more than 20 striae. Leaves remotely 2–3-paired imparipinnate, 30–62 cm long including petioles, the lowest and next the pinnae ternate, upper and terminal pinnae smaller, entire, all leaflets ovate-elliptic, acute or acuminate at apex, cuneate, truncate to subcordate at base, 5.5–10 by 2.8–4.8 cm, herbaceous, 5 or 7 veins branching near base, glabrous on both sides, prominently veined beneath; petiolules 1.5–2 cm long, terminal petiolules up to 6 cm long; petioles 8–12 cm long, glabrous, dilated near base. Inflorescences terminal and axillary, axillary ones sometimes with more than 100 flowers, thyrsiform, glabrous; peduncles 6–12 cm long, glabrous; bracts leafy, sometimes linear; pedicels glabrous, 2–4 cm long; bracteoles linear, small or none. Flowers flat or with slightly reflexed sepals, 2–2.5 cm diam. Sepals 4, elliptic-oblong, acute to acuminate at apex, 15–20 by 2.5–4 mm, white, upper surface glabrous, lower surface glabrous or sparsely pubescent, margins white tomentose. Anthers of outer stamens linear, lateral, 1.5–3 mm long, connectives projected, filaments yellowish, up to 15 mm long, glabrous, filiform, thinner than anthers; anthers of inner stamens linear, lateral or more or less introrse, 3–4 mm long, connectives projected, filaments yellowish, shorter, 2–4 mm long, glabrous, more or less dilated, nearly as broad as anther. Achenes yellowish brown, fusiform, slightly recurved, often tortuous, 8–10 by 1.8–2 mm, slightly compressed, thick-margined, with a longitudinal ridge on each side and a lignified basal projection up to 2 mm long, glabrous, tails 5–7.5 cm long, plumose with ascendant, up to 6 mm long hairs, but shorter towards base.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Clematis eichleri . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 57. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Evergreen climber, drying brown or greyish brown. Stems glabrous, internodes with many striae. Leaves simple, broadly ovate, 8.5–16.5 by 6.5–13.2 cm, cordate at base, acute at apex, entire, chartaceous, 5–7-veins branching near base, glabrous on both surfaces, prominently reticulate beneath; petioles 3.8–10 cm long, conspicuously dilated near base. Inflorescences thyrsiform, more than 30-flowered, axillary ones 5–7-flowered, velvety with erect, brown, often glandular hairs; peduncles 3–6.5 cm long; bracts scaly, sometimes linear, up to 1 cm long; pedicels 3–4.5 cm long; bracteoles scaly, up to 3 mm long, below the middle and almost hidden in bracts. Flowers 2–4 cm diam. Sepals 6, elliptic or densely velvety. Anthers linear, lateral or slightly introrse, 2–2.5 mm long, connectives projected, 2–3.5 mm long, filaments glabrous, 3–4 mm long, as broad as anther, dilated downwards; outer stamens sometimes sterile. Achenes elliptic-rhombic, 6–7 by 4–4.5 mm, compressed, thick-margined, suddenly contracted to base like a short stipe, densely covered with brownish-yellowish, appressed or ascending hairs, tails up to 5 cm long, plumose with ascending, yellowish-brownish, ca 4 mm long hairs, but shorter towards base.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Clematis fulvicoma . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 60. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Deciduous or evergreen herbaceous climber, drying greyish yellow. Stems glabrous, with many striae. Leaves pinnately 5-, in upper leaves often 3-, foliolate, leaflets ovate, 2–5 by 1.2–3.3 cm, round to subcordate at base, obtuse to round at apex, herbaceous, main veins 3–5, inner veins branching above the outer, glabrous on both sides, sometimes prominently veined beneath; petioles 1.5–8 mm long. Inflorescences terminal and axillary, axillary ones racemose, often densely branched, 3 to 10-flowered, glabrous; peduncles glabrous, 1.3–3 cm long; bracts leafy, 7–10 by 6 cm; petioles 2–3 mm long, often 3–5-foliolate, pedicels glabrous, 1.5–5 cm long, bracteoles 1.5–10 by 0.8–6 mm. Flowers flat, 1.2–3 cm diam. Sepals 4, spreading, or slightly reflexed, ovate-lanceolate, acute or obtuse at apex, 8–15 by 3–6 mm, white, upper surface glabrous, lower surface glabrous except white tomentose margins. Anthers linear, lateral, 2–3 mm long, connectives pointed, filaments 2–3 mm long, as long as anther, glabrous. Achenes yellowish brown, broadly elliptic, 4.5–6 by 2.5–3.5 mm, compressed, marginate, pubescent with 1–1.5 mm long hairs, tails 2.5–3 cm long, plumose with spreading, whitish hairs throughout.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Clematis garanbiensis . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 60. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Evergreen climbers, drying brownish. Stems glabrous, internodes with many striae; axillary shoot often with linear scales at base. Leaves ternate, middle leaflets elliptic-ovate to oblong-lanceolate, 5.5–13 by 2.7–4.8 cm, broadly cuneate, round or truncate at base, acute to acuminate at apex, entire, coriaceous, main veins 3 or 5, sometimes 7, branching near base, glabrous on both sides, veins prominent on underside, petiolules 1.2–2.7 cm long, lateral leaflets similar to the middle, shortly petiolulate, petioles 6–12 cm long, glabrous, dilated near base. Inflorescences axillary, thyrsiform or compound thyrsiform, 5- to more than 60-flowered, glabrous, peduncles 3.5–6 cm long, sparsely crisp pubescent, sometimes contracted, a pair of the lowest branches being produced from the base of the inflorescence axis as accessory cymes, glabrous, bracts scaly, minute, 2–3 mm long, pedicels crisp pubescent, 1.5–3 cm long, bracteoles minute, up to 1 mm long. Flowers flat, 2–3 cm diam. Sepals 4, oblong-lanceolate, acute to acuminate at apex, 10–17 by 1.8–4 mm, white to pale green, drying brownish to blackish, upper surface glabrous, lower surface long, appressed hairy or glabrous, margins tomentose with dirty whitish hairs. Anthers linear oblong, lateral, 2.8–3.5 mm long, connectives minutely pointed, filaments drying brownish, 4–6 mm long, glabrous, thinner than anther. Achenes drying blackish to brownish, fusiform to elliptic, often oblique, 5–8 by 2–2.5 mm, compressed, shortly stipitate downwards, tapering to tail upwards, pubescent with ascending hairs, tails 3–4 cm long, plumose with spreading, ca 2.5 mm long hairs.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Clematis meyeniana . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 56. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Evergreen climber, drying blackish. Stems nearly glabrous except in young shoots, internodes porcate with 8–12 ridges. Leaves ternate, middle leaflets ovate, 7–16 by 3.2–7 cm, cordate to truncate at base, acuminate at apex, remotely dentate, chartaceous-herbaceous, 5 veins branching near base, upper surface glabrous or sparsely pubescent, lower surface glabrous, prominently reticulate, petiolules 1–1.5 cm long, lateral leaflets similar to the middle, shortly petiolulate; petioles 4–11 cm, glabrous or sparsely pubescent, dilated near base. Inflorescences axillary, trichotomous, 3–20-flowered, glabrous; peduncles 1–8 cm; bracts small, linear; pedicels glabrous, 1.5–4 cm long; bracteoles minute, sometimes absent. Flower campanulate, 1.5–2.5 cm diam., 1.3–2.0 cm long. Sepals 4, lanceolate, acute to acuminate at apex, reflexed upwards, 10–21 by 3–6 mm, yellowish green, drying blackish to brownish, upper surface glabrous or slightly pubescent, hairs denser in upper part, lower surface glabrous or slightly pubescent, margins tomentose with white hairs. Anthers linear, lateral, 2–4 mm long, hidden in staminal hairs, connectives hardly projected, filaments drying brownish, 5–19 mm long, narrow, pilose with ascending, long hairs except at basal. Achenes drying blackish, elliptic, 3–5.5 by 2–3 mm, compressed, slightly marginate, apiculate downwards like a small stipe, pubescent, tails 3.5–4 cm long, plumose with white ascending ca 3.5 mm long hairs, but shorter towards base.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Clematis sikkimensis . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 52. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Evergreen climber, sometimes up to more than 10 m, drying brownish. Stems glabrous, internodes porcate with 12 or more ridges, sometimes with more small striae. Leaves simple, broadly ovate to lanceolate, 6–21 by 3–17 cm, subcuneate, truncate to cordate at base, acute to acuminate at apex, peltate with petiole attached up to 4 mm distant from basal margin of blade, small leaves usually epeltate, entire, herbaceous to coriaceous, 5–7-veined, veins branching near base, glabrous on both sides, sometimes pubescent along veins; petioles 5–12 cm long, usually glabrous, dilated near base. Inflorescences axillary, thyrsiform, 10–27-flowered; peduncles 5–10 cm, sparsely crisp pubescent; bract linear to linear-oblong; pedicels 3.5–10 cm long, pubescent to subvillose with brownish, soft hairs especially upwards; bracteoles minute, up to 3 mm long, sometimes absent. Flowers 2.5–4 cm diam, sometime unisexual. Sepals 6, sometimes 4, reflexed, elliptic-lanceolate to ovate-oblong, acute at apex, 20–35 by 3.5–7 mm, upper surface glabrous, purplish to dull scarlet, lower surface purplish brown, villose, margins tomentose with dirty white hairs. Stamens erect, anthers linear, lateral or slightly introrse, 2–5 mm long, connective projected, 1–1.5 mm long, filaments drying blackish, 8–16 mm long, glabrous, slightly dilated downwards. Achenes yellowish to brownish, elliptic-rhombic, sometimes oblique, 6–12 by 3.2–7 mm, compressed, thick-margined, contracted to both ends, pubescent, tails 4–6 cm long, plumose with white or yellowish, ascending or spreading, 2–5 mm long hairs, but shorter, appressed or ascending towards base.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Clematis smilacifolia . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 59. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Evergreen sometimes deciduous climber, drying greyish brown. Stems densely branched, pilose with soft, white hairs, internodes porcate with 12 ridges. Leaves 2- or 3-paired-imparipinnate, 14–29 cm including petioles, the lowest pinnae 3-sometimes 5-foliolate, lateral leaflets smaller than terminal ones, upper pinnae ternate or simple, the uppermost pinnae, if present, simple, terminal pinnae simple, all leaflets ovate to elliptic lanceolate, more or less asymmetrical in lateral ones, 2–5.5 by 1.3–3 cm, entire or 1–2-dentate in upper part, subcoriaceous, 3–7-veined, inner veins branching above the outer, upper surface pubescent or glabrous, lower surface reticulate, tomentose to pubescent; petiolules up to 2 cm long; petioles 4.2–7.5 cm long, villose or pilose, dilated at base. Prophylls often at base of axillary shoots or of inflorescences, broadly ovate, up to 2.5 by 2 cm, usually coarsely lobate-dentate, with short petioles. Inflorescences terminal and axillary, thyrsiform or trichasial, or modified from these, 9–85-flowered, upper branches often appearing dichotomous by suppression of a terminal flower, or subumbellate with a main axis and accessory ones by abbreviation of peduncles, actually upto 7 cm long, villose, bracts elliptic to linear; pedicels villose, 1–3 cm long, bracteoles linear, minute. Flowers bisexual, sometimes unisexual, flat, 1.1–2 cm diam. Sepals 4, elliptic or elliptic-oblong, obtuse at apex, 4–8 by 1.8–3.5 mm, whitish to yellowish, entirely tomentose on both sides. Anthers elliptic-oblong, lateral, 1.5–2 mm long, connectives not projected, filaments drying blackish, ovate-elliptic, 4–6 by 2–3 mm, slightly compressed, slightly marginate, tapering to both ends, sometimes with a longitudinal wrinkle on each side, with a slight basal projection, pubescent, tails 2.5–3.5 cm long, plumose with greyish, ascending, ca 2 cm hairs, but shorter and appressed towards base.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Clematis subumbellata . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 53. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Evergreen climber or low climber, drying brownish-greyish. Stems densely covered with short, yellowish, crisp hairs, internodes with more than 12 striae. Leaves ternate, middle leaflets ovate-lanceolate to elliptic, 5.0–10.5 by 2–4.5 cm, round to slightly cordate at base, acuminate at apex, entire or lobate-dentate on upper part, lobes acute, herbaceous or subcoriaceous, 5–7-veined, inner veins branching slightly above the outer, upper surface pubescent especially on veins, lower surface reticulate, densely pilose or tomentose with yellowish hairs especially on veins, petiolules 0.7–2.3 cm long, lateral leaflets similar to the middle, but oblique ovate to ovate-elliptic, outer margins often lobulate, shortly petiolulate, petioles 5–9.5 cm long, yellowish, crisp pubescent dilated near base. Inflorescences axillary, trichotomous or thyrsiform, 5–25-flowered, peduncles 3–4.5 cm long, appressed villose, bracts linear to lanceolate, acuminate, up to 2.6 cm long, pedicels 1–2 cm long, villose, bracteoles linear. Flowers flat, 1.5–1.8 cm diam., drying blackish. Sepals 4, elliptic-oblong, obtuse to acuminate at apex, 8–10 by 2–2.5 mm, white, drying blackish, upper surface glabrous, lower surface tomentose throughout. Anthers linear, lateral, 2–3 mm long, connectives shortly pointed, filaments drying brownish to blackish, 2–4 mm long, glabrous, slightly dilated, tapering to base. Achenes drying brownish to blackish, ovate or ovate-elliptic, 3.5–4 by 3–3.5 mm, compressed, margins not distinct, densely covered with yellowish, appressed hairs, tails 1.5–2.5 cm long, plumose with ascending, yellowish, 1–2 mm long hairs throughout.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Clematis thaiana . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 54. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Evergreen climber, drying blackish. Stems covered with minute crisp hairs, internodes porcate with 6 ridges. Leaves remotely 2-paired-imparipinnate, 21–32 cm including petioles, the lowest pinnae ternate or 3-partite, petiolulate, upper pinnae usually simple, sessile or petiolulate, terminal pinnae simple, tripartite or ternate, all leaflets or leaf-segments elliptic, ovate-elliptic or lanceolate elliptic, more or less asymmetrical in lateral ones, 2–8 by 1–3 cm, acute at base, acute to acuminate at apex, margins entire or serrate with few teeth, herbaceous or coriaceous herbaceous, mian veins 3–7, branching near base, upper surface nearly glabrous except veins, lower surface pubescent especially on veins, petiolules up to 2.2 cm long, petioles 4.5–7 cm long, hardly dilated near base. Inflorescences axillary, trichotomous, 9–13-flowered, peduncles 3–4 cm long, bracts elliptic, pedicels 3.5–4.5 cm long, crisp pubescent to subvillose, bracteoles ovate, 3–4 mm long. Flowers flat, drying blackish, 2–3.5 cm diam. Sepals 4, elliptic-oblong, obtuse at apex, 14–18 by 2.5–5 mm, white, drying blackish, upper surface glabrous, lower surface entirely tomentose with yellowish, incurved or ascending hairs, denser along margins. Anthers elliptic, lateral, 0.8–1 mm long, connectives not projected, filaments drying blackish, 7–10 mm long, glabrous, filiform, thickened at apex, slightly dilated downwards. Achenes drying blackish, broadly ovate, 4–5 by 2.5–3 mm, compressed, hardly marginate, sessile, hispid with long, white hairs, tails 3–4.5 cm long, plumose with ca 2 mm hairs, but shorter towards base.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Clematis thaimontana . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 53. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Tree or shrub, to 10 m tall. Leaves narrowly elliptic to elliptic, sometimes falcate, 8–19 by 3–6.5 cm, base cuneate, apex acute to caudate, petiole to 4 cm. Inflorescence axis to 6 cm long, flower pedicels to 1 cm, bracts quickly caducous. Male flowers with 4 or 5 calyx lobes, ca 1 mm long, free; stamens 8–10, free, apiculate. Female flowers calyx caducous, style circinnate, staminodes present but quickly falling. Drupes on pedicel to 16 mm long, red when mature, ellipsoid, to 14 by 7 mm, surface smooth, tuberculate on dried herbarium material because of the tuberculate pyrene.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Shrub or small tree. Leaves lanceolate or elliptic, 11–37 by 3.5–13 cm, base obtuse to cuneate, apex acuminate, petioles to 13 cm. Male flowers on pedicels to 20 mm long, calyx 3–4(–7) lobed, united at base, lobes broadly triangular, unequal, irregularly serrate, ca 1 mm long, apex acute; stamens 8 or 9, coherent at apex. Female flowers on pedicels to 16 mm long, calyx with 3–5 lobes, similar to those of male flowers but more deeply lobed; ovary glaucous, style and stigmas very short. Drupes on pedicel to 16 mm long, brown, ellipsoid, to 12 by 7 mm, calyx lobes persistent.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Daphniphyllum laurinum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 6. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Tree to 15 m tall. Leaves elliptic or ovate, 11–34 by 4.5–18 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, petioles to 11 cm. Male flowers on pedicels to 25 mm long, calyx lobes free, orbicular, ca 2 by 2 mm, apex rounded; stamens 12, coherent at apex. Female flowers on pedicels to 15 mm long, calyx with 3–5 lobes, free, similar to those of male flowers; ovary glaucous, style and stigmas very short. Drupes on pedicel to 20 mm long, black, ellipsoid, to 12 by 6 mm, calyx lobes persistent.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Daphniphyllum majus . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 6. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Shrub, 2.5 m. Leaves narrowly elliptic, to 26 by 7 cm, base cuneate, apex acute, petioles to 6 cm. Male flowers on pedicels to 25 mm long, calyx lobes free, ovate or elliptic, ca 2 mm long, apex rounded or acute; stamens 12, coherent at apex. Female flowers on pedicels to 15 mm long, calyx with 3–5 lobes, free, similar to those of male flowers; style and stigmas short. Drupes on pedicel to 20 mm long, black, ellipsoid, to 12 by 6 mm, tuberculate, calyx lobes persistent.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Daphniphyllum pierrei . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 7. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Perennial, sometimes annual herbs. Stems erect. Leaves alternate, palmately or pedately lobed, sometimes ternately or subpinnately compound. Inflorescence definite, sometimes indefinite, recemose, paniculate, or modifications of these. Flowers bisexual, zygomorphic. Sepals 5, petaloid, upper one spurred. Petals 4, upper 2 sessile, spurred, nectariferous; lower 2 unguiculate, not nectariferous. Stamens numerous, glabrous, anthers lateral, elliptic to subglobose, connectives not projected. Carpels multiovular. Follicles 3–7, aggregated in a fruit. Seeds several to many in a carpel, lamellate or smooth.</br></br>About 330 species distributed mostly in the northern hemisphere and Africa. In Thailand, 1 species occurs.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Deciduous, perennial herb, 30–150 cm tall, with erect, thick, rhizomes. Stems erect, branched, sparsely covered with white, spreading hairs in lower part, densely covered with curled or ascendant hairs in upper part. Basal and lower cauline leaves pentagonal reniform, 3–25 by 3–25 cm., cordate to deeply sinuate at base, 5–7-fid, segments obovately cuneate, 3-lobate, lobes often lobulate, coarsely dentate, teeth ovate, acute, upper surface sparsely pubescent, lower surface pilose with long, white hairs, petioles 10–45 cm, patent hairy, dilated near base. Middle cauline leaves smaller, shortly petiolate; upper ones cuneate, 3-partite to 3-sect, usually nearly sessile. Inflorescences racemose, 2–8-flowered, branched at lower part, pilose with curled, white, glandular hairs, bracts lanceolate to linear, pedicels 1.8–5 cm, pilose or subvillose, bracteoles 2, alternate, usually at middle of pedicels. Flowers half-open, 15–23 mm diam., 27–35 mm long. Sepals blue or blue violet, densely covered with yellowish hairs outside, glabrous inside; upper one 10–14 mm long, spurs 14–20 mm long; lateral ones broadly elliptic, 10–14 by 5–6 mm; lower ones elliptic, 12–15 by 2–6 mm. Petals concolorous with sepals; upper 2 glabrous, acute to acuminate, bilobate at apex, 11–13 by 5–6 mm, spurs 17–18 mm long; lower 2 obvate, 6–7 by 3–5 mm, barbate above, hispid beneath, bifid, lobes with claws 5–7 mm long. Anthers spherical or elliptic, lateral, ca 1 mm long, dark purple, filaments edentate, dilated downwards. Follicles 3, villose on inner part or throughout, hairs yellowish, ascending, 12–14 mm long, beaks straight, 2.5–4 mm long. Seeds obvate, 1.7–2 mm long, transversely lamellate.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Delphinium siamense . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 49. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Trees or shrubs, usually glabrous. Leaves alternate, often distichous. Flowers axillary, solitary or many in axillary fascicles or cymes, often heterostylous, a pair of bracteoles at base of each pedicel. Calyx campanulate, lobes imbricate in bud. Petals imbricate in bud, clawed, caducous, with a ligulate appendage on the inner face. Staminal tube usually toothed at apex. Ovary with 1ovule in single fertile locule. Styles free or connate. Drupe 1-seeded. Seed with a thin testa; endosperm variable in quantity or absent; embryo straight.</br></br>About 220 species, occurring throughout the tropics and subtropics, mainly in S. America. The leaves of the shrub Erythroxylum coca Lam. are the source of the drug cocaine. It is not native to Thailand and not described in this treatment, but is included in the key. Three species are native to Thailand, easily recognised as belonging to Erythroxylum because of the distinct stipular scars on the branchlets.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Erythroxylum  . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 8. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Shrub or small tree to 7 m high. Stipules to 7 mm long, bicarinate. Leaves glabrous; petiole 3–8 mm long; blade elliptic to obovate, 6–15 by 2–5.5 cm, base cuneate, margin entire, apex obtuse, often emarginate. Flowers in axillary clusters, pedicels 3–10 mm, often considerably longer in fruit; calyx glabrous, tube shorter than lobes, lobes ca 1 mm long, triangular; petals 3–5 mm long, ligule attached in basal half, much shorter than petal; staminal tube equal to or exceeding calyx lobes, filaments either equal, or 5 long and 5 short; styles exceeding the stamens or not, connate to some degree. Drupes red, ellipsoid, often curved, 8–11 by 2.5–5 mm. Seed flattened, 6–8 by 1.5–3 mm.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Erythroxylum cambodianum . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 9. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Tree to 30 m tall, twigs flattened towards ends. Stipules to 6 mm long, bicarinate. Leaves glabrous; petiole 3–7 mm long; blade elliptic to obovate, 4–10 by 2–5 cm, base cuneate, margin entire, apex obtuse, often emarginate. Flowers in several-flowered axillary clusters, pedicels 3–10 mm, often considerably longer in fruit; calyx glabrous, tube shorter than lobes, lobes ca 1 mm long, triangular; petals 3–4 mm long, ligule attached in basal half, much shorter than petal; staminal tube exceeding calyx lobes, stamen filaments either equal, or 5 long and 5 short; styles exceeding the stamens or not, connate to some degree. Drupes red, ellipsoid, often curved, 8–10 by 2.5–4.5 mm. Seed flattened, furrowed, 6–8 by 1.5–3 mm.

description: Shrub to 2 m tall. Stipules to 2.5 mm long, bicarinate. Leaves glabrous; petiole ca 1 mm long; blade oblong-elliptic, 1.9–4.1 by 0.9–1.7 cm, base cuneate or subrounded, margin ?entire, apex emarginate. Flowers in few-flowered axillary clusters, pedicels 3–7 mm; calyx glabrous, tube shorter than lobes, lobes ca 1 mm long, triangular; petals to 3 mm long, ligule much shorter than petal; staminal tube exceeding calyx lobes, filaments either equal; styles exceeding the stamens or not (dolichostylous or brachystylous). Drupes ellipsoid, slightly curved, 7–8 by 3–4 mm.

description: Glabrous shrub with clustered stems, up to 2 m tall; stems greenish brown, 0.5–1 cm diam., woody part 2–3 mm thick; pith spongy, white. Stipules filiform, 1–2 mm long, occasionally divided into 2–3 branches. Leaves oblong or lanceolate, 4–15 by 1.5–3.5 cm, glabrous; apex long acuminate; base cuneate; margin glandular serrate; lateral veins 6–10(–12) per side, arching near margin; scale-like leaves present at tip of branches, 3–5 by 1 mm; petioles 1–2.5 cm long. Flower 3(–4)–merous. Male inflorescence a fascicle of 7–10(–12) flowers, arising slightly lower than the middle of the leaf blade; bracts at the base of pedicels, similar to stipules, ca 1 mm long; pedicels 1–2 mm long; sepals broadly ovate, ca 1.5 by 1 mm, apex acute, glabrous, greenish purple, turning greenish when mature; petals absent; filaments free, glabrous, ca 1 mm long; anthers greyish, 0.2–0.3 mm long; disc cushion-shaped, glabrous, light purplish, 1–2 mm diam., ca 0.5 mm thick. Female inflorescences 1–3 flowered; flowers similar to male, pedicels very short; ovary ca 2 mm long; stigma lobed, recurved. Drupes 1–3, subsessile, ellipsoid, wrinkled when dry, dull pale green turning red when ripe, 7–8 by 4–5 mm; pyrenes 2–3, crustaceous.

description: Trees or shrubs, resting buds with cataphylls. Leaves usually pubescent at first, often becoming glabrous, entire or dentate. Plants monoecious. Inflorescence lateral or terminal, usually cymose, paniculate or fasciculate, pedicels usually thickening distally into the receptacle. Male flowers smaller than the females, with a minute apical opening surrounded by 2–4 decussate pairs of tepals; androecium usually with 4 large outer stamens and up to 4 smaller inner stamens or staminodes that may be rudimentary and ± connate; anthers opening by a single slit, with a filament or subsessile. Female flowers with a minute apical opening surrounded by about 5 decussate pairs of tepals; the inner pairs thickened and glandular; the upper half of the receptacle falling off as a calyptra after anthesis; carpels numerous, stigma almost sessile on the apex of the ovary. Drupes sessile or stipitate. </br></br>According to Philipson’s synopsis of Kibara, the genus comprises 43 species in the Malesian region, most of them in New Guinea. One species is known from Thailand.

description: Understorey tree to 20 m tall, 24 cm diam., rarely a scandent shrub. Leaves opposite (rarely subopposite or whorled), broadly ovate to elliptic oblong, 9–35 by 5–24 cm, coriaceous or chartaceous, base cuneate, rounded or subcordate, apex shortly to long acuminate, margin entire or minutely to coarsely dentate, glabrous or sparingly to rather densely pubescent beneath, midrib and principal lateral veins prominent beneath, lateral veins arched-ascending and meeting within the margin; petiole 5–25 mm, channelled above, glabrous or pubescent. Plants monoecious. Inflorescences axillary, terminal, or cauliflorous, pubescent, cymes solitary or several arising at the same node, varying from simple 3-flowered cymes to complex pleiochasia. Flowers on the lower branches; rachis and lateral branches of female part of the inflorescence stout and becoming woody after anthesis, those of the male parts finer and caducous, up to 20 cm long but often much shorter, pedicels 15–30 mm, gradually thickening below the flowers, those of the male more delicate than those of the female. Male flowers globose, 1.5–2 mm broad, only slightly wider than the pedicel, pubescent; tepals 6–8, apex rounded, usually with 4 outer stamens and up to 4 smaller inner stamens, filaments strap-shaped. Female flowers globose, ca 3–5 mm across; tepals ca 6, with swollen pendulous glands within the ostiole; carpels usually ca 20, stigma short, obtuse. Infructescence enlarged, woody, receptacle ca 20 mm diam., turning yellow-orange at maturity. Drupes ovoid, 15 mm long, shortly stipitate or sessile, blue-black at maturity.

description: Evergreen climber or low climber, drying greyish-brownish. Stems slender, pubescent with brownish, crisp hairs near nodes, internodes porcate with 12–18 ridges. Leaves 2-foliolate, tendrils with a pair of branches, 4–10 cm long, glabrous or pubescent; leaftlets elliptic to ovate elliptic, 4–10 by 1.3–5.5 cm, cuneate, round or truncate at base, obtuse at apex, chartaceous herbaceous, main veins 5, sometimes 3, inner ones branching above the outer, upper surface nearly glabrous slightly reticulate, lower surface sparsely pubescent with brownish crisp hairs glabrate, prominently reticulate; petiolules 2–11 mm, subvillose; petioles 1.2–4 cm long, pubescent with crisp hairs, slightly dilated at base. Inflorescences axillary, usually racemose, 1–7-flowered, densely covered with crisp, brownish hairs, peduncles often contracted; bracts linear or elliptic, sometimes leafy; pedicels 2.5–7 cm long; bracteoles linear, up to 7 mm long. Flowers drying blackish, 2.2–2.8 cm diam. Sepals 4, reflexed, caducous, elliptic ovate, acuminate, 12–20 by 2.5–3.5 mm, white to greenish white, upper surface sparsely pubescent or glabrous, lower surface tomentose to pubescent. Petals 9–14, claviform, 8–25 mm, yellowish green. Stamens dilated, 2.5–4 mm broad, anther-halves linear, nearly parallel, introrse, 2–4 mm long, connective dilated, projected up to ca 0.7 mm, filaments short, thick, 0.3–1 mm long. Achenes narrowly fusiform, slightly bent, 16–22 by 1.5–2.5 mm, slightly thickened downwards, with a short basal projection, without distinct lateral ribs, covered with brownish hairs, beaks elongate, hairs brownish, ascending or appressed.

description: Evergreen climber, robust, drying greyish. Stems pubescent with crisp hairs near nodes, internodes striate with 20 or more striae. Leaves 2-foliolate, tendrils with a pair of branches, 11– 15 cm long, leaflets elliptic or ovate-elliptic, 6.8–17 by 2.8–13 cm, cuneate to subcordate at base, caudately acuminate at apex, coriaceous, main veins 3 to 7, inner ones branching above outer, upper surface glabrous or sparsely pubescent, lower surface prominently reticulate, glabrous or pubescent; petiolules 0.8–2.8 cm long; petioles 3–8 cm long, glabrous or pubescent with crisp hairs, slightly dilated near base. Inflorescences terminal and axillary, thyrsiform or compound thyrsiform, axillary ones 7–25-flowered; peduncles 3–10 cm, sometimes contracted and a pair of the lowest branches from the base appearing as accessory cymes, crisp pubescent, bracts linear, up to 3 mm long; pedicels 1–5.5 cm long, subtomentose or crisp pubescent; bracteoles 1 or 2 in pairs, minute or absent. Flowers drying blackish, 12–20 mm diam. Sepals 4, reflexed, caducous, ovate to obovate-elliptic, acute to obtuse at apex, 4.5–9 by 2–5 mm, yellowish green, upper surface glabrous, lower surface tomentose with greyish white hairs. Petals 10–12, claviform, round to truncate at apex, 8–18 mm. Stamens dilated, 2.5–5 mm, anthers-halves linear, introrse or nearly lateral, divaricate downwards, 2–3 mm long, connectives projected up to ca 0.5 mm, filaments 1.5–3 mm long, as broad as anther. Achenes fusiform, 10–11 by 1.2–2 mm, with a basal projection to 2 mm and a longitudinal wrinkle on each side, pubescent, tails 3–4 cm long, plumose, hairs 3–4 mm long, ascending or spreading, white, throughout.

description: Evergreen climber, drying yellowish-brown. Stems glabrous or sparsely pubescent with brownish, crisp hairs near nodes, internodes porcate with ca 12 ridges. Leaves 2-foliolate, tendrils with a pair of branches, 6–9 cm long, leaflets elliptic or ovate-elliptic, 6–13 by 3.5– 8 cm, subcordate, truncate, sometimes cordate at base, shortly caudate at apex, chartaceous herbaceous, main veins 5–7, branching near base, or inner one higher than the outer, upper surface nearly glabrous, lower surface glabrous, reticulate; petiolules 1.2–2 cm; petioles 3.2–8 cm long, glabrate, hardly dilated at base. Inflorescences terminal and axillary, thyrsiform, axillary ones 20–30-flowered; peduncles 4–11 cm long, crisp pubescent, sometimes glabrate; bracts minute, linear, pubescent or glabrous; pedicels 1–2.8 cm long, pubescent or glabrate; bracteoles linear, minute or absent. Flowers drying blackish, 1.2–1.5 cm diam. Sepals 4, reflexed, caducous, ovate-elliptic, acute at apex, 8–13 by 2.5–3 mm, green or purplish green, upper surface nearly glabrous, lower surface pubescent. Petals 7–10, claviform or spathulate, obtuse to round at apex, 6–10 mm, yellowish green. description: Annual or perennial herbs. Roots fasciculate. Leaves alternate, pedately, or subpinnately lobate to sect, or compound, rarely simple; petioles dilated downwards into the sheath. Inflorescences definite, loosely corymbiform or modified from this, or single-flowered. Flowers bisexual, actinomorphic, heterochlamydeous, usually opening flat. Sepals 3 or 5, usually sepaloid. Petals 3, 5, or more, petaloid, usually larger than sepals, with 1, rarely to 3 nectaries. Stamens numerous, anthers lateral or extrorse. Carpels uniovular, ovule basal, ascending. Achenes many, aggregated; pericarps thick, usually without veins on lateral sides.</br></br>About 650 species in all continents. Three species in Thailand.

description: Annual or biennial herbs, 25–45 cm tall, without rhizomes. Stems erect, densely hispid, hairs spreading, sometimes reflexed in lower part, ascending in upper part. Leaves: Basal and lower cauline leaves ternate, middle leaflets 8.5–9 long including petiolules 2.5–3 mm, 3-sect or –partite, middle segments 3-fid to -lobate, lateral ones 2-partite to –fid, lateral leaflets 6.5–7.5 cm long including petiolules 5–10 mm, 2-sect to -fid, segments 2–4-fid, lobes cuneate, irregularly, coarsely incised-dentate, teeth lanceolate to ovate-lanceolate, acute, upper surface sparsely pilose with spreading, long hairs or glabrate, lower surface with long, spreading hairs especially on veins; petioles 10–13 cm long, hispid, with sheathing bases. Cauline leaves 3–4, similar to the basal, but smaller, simpler, shortly petiolate. Inflorescences loosely corymbiform, 7–17-flowered, pedicels 1–3 cm, hispid. Flowers nearly flat, 6–10 mm diam. Sepals 5, reflexed, narrowly ovate, round to obtuse at apex, 3–5 by 1.5–2 mm, green, upper surface glabrous, lower surface hispid. Petals 5, yellow, narrowly obovate, round at apex, 4–5 by 1.8–2 mm, upper surface glabrous, with a nectar flap, lower surface glabrous. Anthers elliptic, lateral, 1–2 mm long, connective not projected, filaments filiform, 1.5–3 mm long. Receptacles elliptic to elliptic-oblong, hispid, 3.5– 4 by 1.8–2 mm in flower; swollen, 8–13 by 2.5–3 mm infruit. Achenes many, in an ellipsoidal head, 12–15 by 6.5–8 mm; oblique obovate-elliptic, 2.5–3 by 0.8–2 mm, compressed, marginate along both, especially along the ventral sides, glabrous, beaks short, narrowly triangular, dilated at base.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Biennial herbs, 10–45 cm tall, without rhizomes. Stems glabrous, fistulose, sometimes slightly hairy in upper part, well-branched. Leaves: Basal leaves glabrous, 3–20, orbicular to reniform, 2.5–8 by 3.5–9 cm, 3-sect to -partite, middle segment 3-fid lateral ones obliquely 2- or 3-fid or -partite, lobes 3-lobulate or lobulate-dentate, lobules with 2–4 round teeth; petioles glabrous, 4.5–10 cm long, sheathing near base. Cauline leaves 5–16, glabrous, lower ones ternate, segments lanceolate-elliptic to oblong, 3.8–4 by 0.8–1 cm, sometimes 3 lobate-dentate at apex; petioles up to 8; upper one bract-like, usually entire, elliptic-oblong, 1.8–3.5 cm long. Inflorescences corymbiform, many-flowered; pedicels 5–27 mm, glabrous or sparsely pubescent. Flowers flat, 5–8 mm diam. Sepals 5, usually slightly reflexed, elliptic, acuminate at apex, 2.5–3 by 1.2–1.8 mm, green, upper surface glabrous, lower surface hairy, sometimes nearly glabrous later. Petals 5, yellow, obovate, obtuse to round at apex, 2.5–4 by 1.3–1.8 cm, upper surface glabrous, with a nectar pit, lower surface hairy, sometimes nearly glabrous later. Anthers elliptic, lateral, 0.2–0.5 mm long, connectives not projected, filaments narrow linear, 1–3 mm long. Receptacles ellipsoid, hispid or glabrous, 1.5–4 by 0.8–2.5 mm in flower; swollen, 2–12 by 1–4 mm in fruit. Achenes 80–230 in an ellipsoidal head, 8–12 by 3–5 mm; broad obovate, 0.8–1.2 by 0.8–1 mm, margins not distinct, swollen, glabrous, often transversely wrinkled, beaks very short.

description: Evergreen perennial herbs, 25–80 cm tall, without rhizome. Stems erect, sometimes decumbent, loosely branched upward, hispid, hairs white, spreading or ascending in lower part, ascending or appressed in upper part. Leaves: Basal leaves 1–6, ternate, sometimes 3-sect, 3.5– 7.5 by 4.5–9 cm, middle leaflets obovate, cuneate at base, 3-lobed in upper part, sometimes petiolulate, lateral leaflets obliquely obovate or broadly-obovate, cuneate or broadly cuneate at base, 2-partite or -fid, sometimes petiolulate, all lobes coarsely incised dentate, teeth ovate, acute, upper surface sparsely hispid, lower surface densely hispid; petioles 6–20 cm long, hispid, sheathing downwards. Cauline leaves 2–4, similar to the basal, but smaller, simpler, shortly petiolate or nearly sessile, bracts linear or 3-partite, entire. Inflorescences loose, leafy, corymbiform, 3–7-flowered; pedicels 2–10 cm, hispid with ascending or appressed hairs. Flowers nearly flat, 1–1.6 cm diam. Sepals 5, spreading, ovate-elliptic, acuminate at apex, 4–5 by 1.8– 3 mm, green, upper surface glabrous, lower surface hispid. Petals 5, yellow, obovate-oblong to oblong, obtuse at apex, 7–8 by 3–6 mm, upper surface glabrous, with a nectar flap, lower surface glabrous. Anthers elliptic or obovate-elliptic, lateral or extrorse, 0.6–1.5 mm long, often recurved, connectives not projected, filaments filiform, recurved, 2–3.5 mm long. Receptacles obovoid-globose, hispid, 1.5–2 by 1–1.5 mm in flower; 2–4 by 1.8–3 mm in fruit. Achenes 50–70 in a globose head, 1–1.2 by 1–1.2 cm, oblique obovate, 3–4 by 2–2.7 mm, compressed, marginate, glabrous, beaks narrowly triangular, straight, up to 1 mm long.

description: Erect, twining, or trailing herbs, glabrous or hairy, with short perennial rootstock; roots many, tuberous, fusiform; stem in lower part with sheathing cataphylls; prophyll inconspicuous (fig. 1). Leaves alternate, opposite, or in whorls; petiole at base somewhat pulvinate, not sheathing; blade simple, ovate or (narrowly) elliptic, margin entire, apex acute-acuminate, 6–13-veined from the base, and curved to the apex, secondary venation fine, transverse and scalariform between the primary veins. Inflorescences axillary, sessile or pedunculate; flowers few, subumbellate, raceme-like, bracts narrow; buds elongate, 5–55 mm long, acute. Flowers with articulate pedicels, the part below articulation persistent; bracts narrow, acute, margin entire, (sub)persistent; perianth of 4 tepals; tepals imbricate, free, narrow (the outer ones narrower), out curved or reflexed at anthesis, apex mostly acute (-acuminate); longitudinally striped and veined; persistent in fruit; stamens 4, anthers with the thecae dorsally attached to a long connective with a petaloid outgrowth, the two thecae either apically with 1 common additional appendage and the apices of all 4 stamens connivent, or additional appendage lacking, filaments short, bases shortly connate and adnate to tepals; ovary superior, ovoid, small, 1.5–3(–4) mm long, 1(–3) mm wide, glabrous, one-celled, ovules few or many, basally attached, stigma minute, sessile. Fruit ripening green, glabrous, capsular, opening with 2 valves from the apex, elongate, apex acute or shortly beaked; pericarp thin; perianth persistent. Seeds 3–20, red or brown, mostly elongate, (5–)7–12(–15) mm long, (2–)3–4 mm wide, often shortly beaked (globose in S. kerrii, ca 5 mm across), longitudinally ridged; aril consisting of finger-like or vesicular lobes, covering the base of the seed; funicle long, pseudo-funicle lacking.</br></br>A genus of about 20 species distributed in China and Japan, through Malesia east to Australia; 11 species in Thailand.

description: Twiner, stems 2–3(–4) m long, glabrous, sometimes precociously flowering on erect shoots. Leaves alternate; petiole 4–6.5 cm long; blade ovate or broadly ovate, 6–8 by 3–4.5 cm, 9–11-veined, base (shallowly) cordate or truncate. Inflorescences borne in the axils of scale like leaves or in the axils of distal leaves, 1–2(–3)-flowered, sessile or on short peduncles to 5 mm long; bracts 8–10 mm long. Flowers: pedicel 5–20 mm long; tepals narrowly triangular, 20–25 by 4–6 mm; stamens (15–)20–27 mm long, ca 2 mm broad, filaments ca 2 mm long, anthers 8–13 mm long, ridge separating the thecae fleshy, smooth and somewhat undulate, ca 1 mm high, petaloid outgrowth of the connective subulate, 8–14 mm long, additional appendage lacking. Fruit 20–30 by 13–16 mm. Seeds 5–6(–10), light brown, 10–12 by ca 4 mm; aril with finger-like lobes.</br></br>Fieldnotes.— The tepals are recorded as pink or yellowish pink or greenish purple; stamens as purple or pink; the tuberous roots as 10–30 cm long, ca 1 cm thick.

description: Erect, then, later, weakly proliferating and subscandent herb to 1m tall, glabrous, the proliferating apical part usually sterile. Leaves alternate; petiole 4–17 cm long; blade (broadly) ovate, 9.5–17 by 5.5–10.5 cm, base cordate; (11–)13–17(–19)-veined. Flowers: pedicel 10–25 mm long, tepals narrowly triangular, (15–)18–22 by 3–5 mm; stamens 18–20 mm long, filaments 1.5–2 mm long, anthers 6–8 mm long, ridge separating the thecae fleshy, smooth, ca 1 mm high, petaloid outgrowth of the connective subulate, ca 7 mm long, minute additional appendage sometimes present. Fruit 25–35 by 12–15 mm. Seeds 3–5, dark pink, 10–12 by 3–4 mm; aril finger-like lobed.</br></br>Fieldnotes.— The tepals are recorded as pink or yellowish pink or purple inside and paler outside; stamens as pink and yellowish; petaloid outgrowth of the connective as green at apex; the tuberous roots as 10–30 cm long, ca 1 cm thick.

description: Herb, erect or weakly climbing or trailing, 20–30(–60) cm tall, glabrous, sometimes branched. Leaves alternate; petiole 1–5 cm long; blade (broadly) ovate, 4–7 by 2–4.5 cm, base cuneate, truncate or shallowly cordate; 7–9-veined. Flowers: pedicel 3–5 mm long; tepals narrowly triangular, 8–10 by 2–2.5 mm; stamens 6.5–7(–9) by ca 0.5 mm, filaments ca 1 mm long, anthers 2.2–3 mm long, ridge separating the thecae smooth, petaloid outgrowth of the connective subulate, 3–4 mm long, additional appendage lacking. Fruit 16–20 by ca 7 mm. Seeds 1–3, dark brown, ca 7 by 3 mm; aril finger-like lobed.</br></br>Fieldnotes.— The tepals are recorded as pink or white or dirty purplish-greenish; the stamens as white; the roots as 10–16 cm long, ca 1 cm thick.

description: Erect then,later, climbing or trailing herb to 60 cm long, glabrous, rarely branched, sterile towards apex when climbing. Leaves alternate; petiole 5–15 cm long; blade broadly or narrowly ovate, 11–15 by 5–11 cm, base cordate; 11–15(–17)-veined. Seeds 3–6, pink-red, 10–12 by 3–4 mm; aril finger-like lobed.</br></br>Fieldnotes.— The tepals are recorded as whitish green or pinkish white, with green veins; the stamens as yellowish green, the petaloid outgrowth of the connective as yellow; the tuberous roots as 10–40 cm long, 1–1.5 cm thick.

description: Twiner 1–2 m tall, glabrous, sparsely branched. Leaves alternate, seldom opposite; petiole 4–12 cm long; blade (narrowly) ovate, 6–21 by 2.5–12.5 cm, sometimes slightly rough, base (shallowly or) broadly cordate; 11–17(–19)-veined. Inflorescences 1- many-flowered, pedunculate; peduncle 1–10(–18) cm long, not fused with the petiole; bracts 6–20 mm long. Flowers: pedicel 10–20 mm long; tepals narrowly triangular, 17–30 mm by 5(–7) mm; stamens 18–25 mm long, filaments ca 2 mm long, anthers 12–15 mm long, with narrow sterile thecal remnants up to the apex, ridge separating the thecae smooth, 1–1.5 mm high, petaloid outgrowth of connective gradually tapering, 6–10 mm long, additional appendage lacking. Seeds 5–10, dark red, 10–15 by 3–3.5 mm; aril finger-like lobed.</br></br>Fieldnotes.— The tepals are recorded as pink, brown-pink or dark brownish red; the stamens as reddish maroon; the tuberous roots as 10–60(–80) cm long, 1–1.5 cm thick.

description: Twiner or trailer to 1 m tall, glabrous, regularly precociously flowering, occasionally branched. Leaves alternate; petiole 3.5–6.5 cm long; blade cordate or triangular-ovate, 5–11 by 4–7 cm, base shallowly cordate or truncate; 7–9-veined. Inflorescences 1-flowered, borne in the axils of leaf-like scales or leaves, sessile; bracts ca 7 mm long. Flowers: pedicel 5–17 mm long; tepals narrowly ovate, 15–20 by 3–5 mm; stamens 13–15 mm long, ca 2 mm wide, filaments ca 1 mm long, anthers ca 5 mm long, ridge separating the thecae smooth, 0.5 mm high or less, petaloid outgrowth of the connective ca 12 mm long with involute margins, additional appendage lacking. Fruit ca 13 by 10 mm. Seeds 3–6, light brown, 7–8 by 3–4 mm; aril finger like lobed.</br></br>Fieldnotes.— The tepals are recorded as pink or dark purple, outside green-veined; the tuberous roots as 10–30 cm long, ca 1 cm thick.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Twiner (50–)100 cm tall, finely hairy all over, branched. Leaves alternate; petiole 1.5–4 cm long; blade broadly ovate, 4–7 by 3–5 cm, base cordate; (9–)13–17-veined. Inflorescences axillary or rarely fused with petiole, 1–4-flowered, pedunculate; peduncle 1–2.5 cm long; bracts ca 5 mm long. Flowers: pedicel 15–45 mm long; tepals narrowly ovate, 10–12 by 3–4 mm, margin with short hairs; stamens 8–12 mm long, ca 2 mm wide, filaments less than 0.5 mm long, anthers 2–4 mm long; ridge separating the thecae ca 0.5 mm high, smooth, continuing above the thecae as a ca 1 mm high ridge on the outgrowth of the connective, with a distal, ca 1 mm long, patent, elongate, yellow body, petaloid outgrowth of the connective narrowly triangular, ca 6 by 2 mm, somewhat folded, additional appendage lacking. Fruit ovoid, 12–14 by 8–10 mm, glabrous. Seeds 1–3, light brown, nearly globose, ca 5 mm across; aril broadly finger-like lobed.</br></br>Fieldnotes.— The tepals are recorded as yellowish purple; the stamens as dark purple or maroon, the outgrowth of the connective deep purple-blackish; the tuberous roots as 5–10 cm long, ca 1 cm thick.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Stemona kerrii . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 85. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Twiner 2–6 m tall, glabous, ± branched, regularly precociously flowering. Leaves alternate, opposite, or whorled; petiole 5–9 cm long; blade (broadly) ovate, 12–17 by 8–10 cm, base (shallowly) cordate, 9–13-veined. Inflorescences axillary to lower scale-like leaves (precociously flowering) or fused with the petiole of leaves for (0.2–)0.5–1.5 cm, 1–3-flowered, pedunculate; peduncle 3–8 cm long; bracts 5–10 mm long. Flowers: pedicel 5–15 mm long; tepals narrowly triangular, 55–65 by 12–20 mm; stamens 50–60 mm long, filaments ca 5 mm long, anthers 17–20 by ca 5 mm, ridge separating the thecae smooth, ca 2 mm high, petaloid outgrowth of connective conical, 27–30 mm long, additional appendage 5–7 mm long. Fruit (narrowly) ovoid, 30–40 by 20–30 mm. Seeds 10–12 (ovules 20–25), dark brown, ca 15 by 2.5–3 mm; aril finger-like lobed.</br></br>Fieldnotes.— The tepals are recorded as green or yellowish green with dark green and purple-red veins towards the tips outside, with purple-red stripes inside, the stamens as purple at base and yellowish green towards the apex, the anthers as red-brown; the tuberous roots as 40–50 cm long, 2–4 cm thick. The flowers have a carrion smell.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Twiner 1–1.5 m tall, or sometimes erect herb ca 30 cm tall, glabrous. Leaves alternate; petiole ca 2 cm long; blade ovate, 4–7 by 2–3.5 cm, base subtruncate, 5–9-veined. Inflorescences 1–3(–6)-flowered, sessile; bracts ca 4 mm long. Flowers: pedicel ca 4 mm long; tepals narrowly ovate, 6–8 by ca 2 mm; stamens 7–8 mm long, filaments 1.3–2 mm long, anthers 2–2.5 mm long, ridge ca 0.5 mm high, petaloid outgrowth of the connective subulate, 3–4 mm long, additional appendage 1.5–2.5 mm long. Fruit ovoid, ca 20 by 10 mm. Seeds 1–2, brown, ca 10 by 3 mm broad; aril irregularly vesicular-lobed.</br></br>Fieldnotes.— The tepals are recorded as dark red or purple-black, contrasting with white pollen shed from the anthers, the outgrowth of the connective as almost black; the tuberous roots as 10–20 cm long, ca 1 cm thick.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert
bibliographicCitation: Stemona pierrei . Flora of Thailand. Vol. 11. Part 1, 2011. Pg. 88. Accessed 2022-04-21

description: Erect or procumbent, somewhat branched herb to 30 cm tall, glabrous. Leaves alternate; petiole 2–5 cm long; blade ovate or narrowly ovate, 5.5–12 by 2.5–7.5 cm, base cuneate, rounded, or truncate, 5–7-veined. Inflorescences 1–5-flowered, sessile; bracts ca 3.5 mm long. Flowers: pedicel 4–10 mm long; tepals narrowly ovate, 10–15 by 2–3.5 mm; stamens 9–10 mm long, filaments less than 0.5 mm long, anthers 5–6 mm long, ridge separating the thecae fleshy, smooth, ca 0.5 mm high, petaloid outgrowth of the connective smooth, subulate, ca 7 mm long, additional appendage 1–1.5 mm long. Fruit (immature) ca 15 by 6 mm. Seeds 2–4, brown, ca 11 by 2 mm; aril vesicular-lobed.</br></br>Fieldnotes.— The tepals are recorded as dark purple, greenish-veined; the tuberous roots as 10–25 cm long, ca 1 cm thick.

description: Twiner 2–5 m tall, branched, glabrous. Leaves opposite or whorled, often alternate in the lower part of the stem; petiole 6–10 cm long; blade narrowly or broadly ovate, 10–21 by 5–12 cm, base (shallowly) cordate, 13–15-veined. Inflorescences axillary, 1- many-flowered, pedunculate; peduncle 0.8–3.5 cm long; bracts 5–25 mm long. Flowers: pedicels 5–18 mm long; tepals narrowly triangular, 25–35 by 5–6 mm; stamens ca 30 mm long; filaments 1–2 mm long; anthers ca 9 mm long, ridge separating the thecae smooth, 1–1.5 mm high, petaloid outgrowth of connective conical, ca 20 mm long, additional appendage 5–6 mm long. Fruit (narrowly-) ovoid, 20–45 by 8–25 mm. Seeds 10–20, brown, 10–12 mm long; aril finger-like lobed.</br></br>Fieldnotes.— The inner surface of the tepals is recorded as yellowish green with brownish red, the outer surface as yellowish green with green stripes towards the apex; the stamens as brownish red and yellowish green at the apex; the tuberous roots as 10–30 cm long, 2–3 cm thick. The flowers have an antiseptic smell.

description: Erect or decumbent branched herbs with short crowded rootstock, leafy shoots several years of age; roots lacking tubers; lower part of stem with sheathing cataphylls often with fimbriate margins; prophyllum present at point of ramification; in erect plants the upper branches often leaning over. Leaves alternate, subdistichous; petiole slightly sheathing at base or not; blade simple, ovate-oblong or elliptic, margin entire, apex acute-acuminate, lateral veins 2–4 pairs, curved, one pair basal, venation finely trabeculate. Inflorescences axillary, pedunculate, with a few to ca 40 flowers arranged in clusters or raceme-like, only 1 or 2 flowers at apex at anthesis; buds (depressed) globose. Flowers small, perfect or functionally unisexual with some reduction of one sex and some dimorphism; pedicel filiform, stiff, articulate, persistent below articulation; bracts narrow, margins fringed, acute, persistent; perianth of 4 tepals, imbricate, almost free, often recurved; stamens 4, free, filaments at base shortly adnate to tepals; anther comprising 2 dorsifixed thecae, horizontal or curved over the apex of the filament, connective broad or narrow, without appendages; ovary superior or semi-inferior, green, ovoid, minute, ca 0.5 mm diam., one-celled, ovules 2–4, placentation apical, style lacking, stigma minute, sessile, 1 (but see the note under Stichoneuron membranaceum). Fruit elongate, apex acute or beaked, green, capsular with 1–4 seeds; pericarp thin; perianth persistent. Seeds large, brown or reddish brown, broadly ellipsoid, (irregularly) longitudinally ridged, aril (elaiosome) of 5–8 finger-like hyaline appendages or irregularly shaped, surrounding seed to about halfway; funicle shorter than the seed, pseudo-funicle (always present?) as long as the fruit.</br></br>A genus of 5 species distributed in NE India, northern Burma south to Peninsular Malaysia. Three species in Thailand.

description: Several-branched low herb, the branches ± woody at base, 20–50(–100) cm long, decumbent, trailing or hanging, growing on vertical limestone rock; most parts (except upper leaf surface, pedicels and flowers) finely hairy, hairs 0.5–1 mm long. Leaves: petiole 2–5(–10) mm long, not sheathing at base; blade ovate or subcircular in outline, 1.5–6 by 1.5–5 cm, base cordate, veins 4(–7) broadly arching from (near) the base to near the apex; prophyll 1–2 mm long. Inflorescences: peduncle glabrescent, 1.5–3.5 cm long, flowers up to 40 in a short, dense raceme, to 15 mm long, sometimes ramified and producing secondary peduncles to 2 cm long; bracts ovate-oblong, acute-acuminate, 1.5–2 by 1–1.5 mm. Flowers: corolla red, 4–5 mm diam.; pedicel 10–15(–20) mm long, persistent part 5–10 mm long, glabrous; tepals ovate-elliptic, 2–3 by 1.5–2 mm, acute(-acuminate) abaxially glabrous, adaxially sparsely or densely set with red hairs less than 0.5 mm long; filaments reddish or purplish, closely adhering, forward directed, stout, 1–1.5 by ca 0.5 mm, hairy, anthers yellow or orange, ca 0.5 mm diam. Fruit narrowly ovoid, (5–)10–12 by 5(–7) mm, glabrous, apex narrow, ± 2-lobed; fruiting pedicel ca 15 mm long. Seeds 1 or 2, reddish or purple-brown, ca 5 by 3 mm, ridges straight, aril wide, irregularly lobed, reaching more than halfway up the seed; funicle short; pseudo-funicle distinct, nearly as long as fruit.</br></br>Fieldnotes.— Flowers red; fruit green.

description: Slender, erect herb (20–)30–80 cm tall, with few branches; stem, petiole and leaves thinly hairy or glabrous. Leaves: petiole 5–10 mm long, sparsely hairy, slightly sheathing at base; blade (ob)ovate or narrowly elliptic, 9–10(–12) by 3–4(–5) cm, base obtuse or shortly cuneate, lateral veins 3 (or 4) pairs; prophyll ca 5 mm long. Inflorescences: subglabrous; peduncle slender, somewhat curved downward, 3–7(–10) cm long; few to densely (c.40) flowered, raceme to 3 cm long; bracts with ± fimbriate margin, ca 2 mm long. Flowers: corolla pinkish brown or reddish purple, 6–8 mm diam.; pedicel 10–15 mm long, persistent part 5–8 mm long; tepals lanceolate, strongly reflexed, 3–4 by ca 2 mm, with a slender appendage 4–7 mm long at apex, abaxially glabrous, adaxially papillose, papillae up to 0.5 mm long; stamens 1.5–2 mm long; filaments forward directed, stout, 1–1.5 mm long, reddish purple, glabrous or papillose; anthers yellow (or purple?). Fruit 20–45 by 7–10 mm, 5(–10) mm beaked; fruiting pedicel ca 15 mm long. Seeds 2–4, brown, ca 7 by 4 mm, ridges straight, aril lobes straight, finger-like; funicle and pseudo funicle not seen.

description: Erect herb 30–60 cm tall, with few branches; stem, petiole and leaves sparsely hairy. Leaves: petiole 5(–7) mm long, inconspicuously sheathing at base, blade narrowly ovate-oblong or elliptic-oblong, glabrous, except veins on lower surface sparsely hairy, 6–12 by 1.5–5.5 cm, base broadly rounded or shortly cuneate, lateral veins 3 (or 4) pairs; prophyll ca 0.5 cm long. Inflorescences: subglabrous; peduncle straight, 0.5–1.5 cm long, with few hairs at base; flowers 5–25, in condensed raceme up to 1 cm long; bracts 1–2 mm long. Flowers: corolla greenish, ca 6 mm diam; pedicel (2–)5–7 mm long, persistent part 2–4 mm long; tepals oblong, patent and slightly reflexed, 3–4 by 1–1.5 mm, apex acuminate for ca 1 mm, abaxially green, glabrous, adaxially yellowish green, sparsely or densely hairy with pale purplish hairs 0.5(–1) mm long; stamens ca 1.5 mm long; filaments patent, erect, greenish or purple, 1(–1.2) mm long, glabrous or finely papillose; anthers ca 0.5 mm long, yellow or orange. Fruit ca 30 by 10 mm, with a 5 mm long beak; fruiting pedicel ca 7 mm long. Seeds (1 or) 2, (dark) brown, ca 9 by 5–6 mm, ridges straight, aril lobes straight, finger-like; funicle short, pseudo-funicle present.

description: Pernnial herbs, often with rhizomes; roots fibrous, sometimes tuberous. Stems often striate. Leaves alternate, ternately or pinnately compound, rarely simple, leaflets lobate, crenate upwards, petioles sheathing at base. Inflorescences terminal, usually paniculiform, corymbiform, or modified from these, several to many-flowered. Flowers generally small, bisexual or unisexual, actinomorphic. Sepals 4, or more, often caducous. Petals none. Stamens numerous, glabrous, anthers lateral, filaments filiform or clavate. Carpels uniovular, ovule pendulous. Achenes few to many, with longitudinal ribs on lateral sides, beaks usually persistent.</br></br>About 370 species distributed in the north hemisphere, and also in Africa, South America and Malesia. Four species and 1 variety in Thailand.

description: Perennial, evergreen, rhizomatous herbs 43–100 cm tall. Stems erect, a little branched upwards, leafy, glabrous, striate. Basal and lower cauline leaves 1–3, 7–10 cm long, glabrous, bi- or triternate, leaflets broadly ovate to obovate, 1–3 by 0.9–3.5 cm, slightly cordate to round at base, 3-lobed, lobes entire, 3-lobulate-crenate or 5–7-crenate-dentate, teeth round or obtuse, mucronate, coriaceous, upper surface glabrous, slightly reticulate, lower surface glaucous, prominently reticulate, glabrous, petioles 6–13 cm long , sheaths auriculate, slightly fissured or entire. Upper cauline leaves smaller, simpler, nearly sessile. Inflorescences corymbose or subpaniculate, glabrous, dichotomous by unequal elongation of branches, 5–20-flowered, pedicels 2–13 mm long, bracts minute, linear, sometimes 3-partite. Flowers bisexual, flat, with caducous sepals and spreading stamens, 4–7 mm diam. Sepals 4, ovate-elliptic, obtuse or slightly acute at apex, 2.5–3 by 1.5–2 mm, white, drying blackish, glabrous on both sides. Stamens as long as, or longer than sepals, anthers elliptic, 0.8–1.2 mm long, sometimes tortuose, connectives hardly projected, filaments drying blackish, clavate, glabrous, 2–3.5 mm long, as broad as, or slightly broader than anther, more or less rugulose. Achenes 3–9 in a head, drying black, ovoid to obovoid, slightly compressed, sessile, 2–3.5 by ca 1.2 mm, glabrous, 2–4 longitudinally costate on each side, abruptly contracted to a narrow, hamate beak upwards, 0.5–0.8 mm long.

description: Evergreen perennial, rhizomatous herb, 0.9–2 m tall, often robust. Stems erect, branched upwards, leafy, glabrous, slightly striate. Basal and lower cauline leaves several, 14–55 cm, 3–6-times pinnately ternate; leaflets ovate-orbicular, ovate-elliptic or obovate-orbicular, 1.5–3.5 by 1–3.5 cm, round to cordate at base, 3–7-crenate-lobate, lobes entire, apiculate, herbaceous, upper surface glabrous, lower surface slightly reticulate, glabrous; petiolules 6–20 mm long; petioles 6–17 cm long, glabrous, sheaths membranaceous, shallowly fissured. Upper cauline leaves smaller, simpler, shortly petiolate. Inflorescences paniculate, with numerous flowers, glabrous, lower bracts leafy, upper ones linear, small; pedicels 3–20 mm long. Flowers bisexual, sometimes male, flat, 8–10 mm diam. Sepals 4, caducous, oblong, obtuse to acute at apex, 3.5– 5 by 1.5–2.5 mm, white or slight bluish, drying blackish, glabrous on both sides. Stamens as long as, or longer than sepals, anthers linear, 2.5–3 mm long, sometimes twisted, connectives projected, filaments drying blackish, filiform, 1.5–5 mm long. Achenes 1–7 in a head, drying blackish, obovoid-ellipsoid or ellipsoid, swollen, slightly compressed, sessile, 2.2–4 by 1.2–1.5 mm, thick, glabrous, 1–3 longitudinally costate on each side, abruptly constricted to a beak, beaks up to 1.2 mm long, narrowly arrowhead-shaped, nearly straight or slightly curved, sometimes folded at base.

description: Perennial herbs 18–60 cm. Stems erect, striate, glabrous. Basal and lower cauline leaves 1–3, 5.5–11 cm, glabrous, 2–3-ternate, leaflets flabellate, broadly ovate to obovate, 1–2.3 by 1.2– 2.3 cm, subcordate to cuneate at base, 3-lobed, lobes 2–3-lobulate-crenate, teeth round to obtuse, apiculate, subcoriaceous, upper surface glabrous, lower surface glabrous, glaucous, reticulate; petioles 6.5–11 cm long, sheaths auriculate, entire or slightly laciniate. Upper cauline leaves smaller, usually 3-foliolate; petiole up to 4.5 mm long. Inflorescences corymbose panicles, glabrous, 10–50-flowered, bracts ternate or simple, often minute, pedicels 2–3.5 cm long. Flowers drying blackish, bisexual, flat, 10–30 mm diam. Sepals 4, sometimes 5, elliptic-oblong, 4–8 by 1.8–3 mm, white to greenish white, glabrous, sometimes reflexed. Stamens shorter than sepals, anthers oblong-elliptic, 0.7–1 mm long, connectives not projected, filaments filiform, 1.5–2 mm long, thinner than anther, thickened at apex. Achenes 20–50 in an oblong to subfusiform head, slightly compressed, sessile, 3–4.5 by 1.5–2 mm, glabrous, convex on dorsal and ventral sutures, 2-costate on each side, tapering gradually to a long, curved beak.
creator: Rachun Pooma & Sawita Yooprasert

description: Perennial, evergreen, rhizomatous herbs 25–85 cm tall. Stems erect, glabrous, striate, leafy, loosely branched. Basal and lower cauline leaves 1–4, 2.5–11 cm long, including petioles, glabrous, ternate, leaflets rotundate-reniform, 1.5–5.5 by 2–7 cm, cordate or broadly cordate at base, shallowly 5–7-lobate, lobes coarsely low crenate, teeth round or obtuse, apiculate, chartaceous-coriaceous, upper surface slightly reticulate, glabrous, lower surface strongly reticulate, slightly glaucous, glabrous; petioles 3.5–14 cm long, sheaths often auriculate, slightly dissected. Cauline leaves 2–4, similar to the basal, but smaller, simpler and shortly petiolate, upper ones often simple. Inflorescences loosely corymbose, 2–7-flowered, glabrous; peduncles 2–10 cm; bracts elliptic to linear, usually entire; pedicels 1.5–7.2 cm long. Flowers bisexual, flat, 1–1.5 cm diam. Sepals 4, elliptic, obtuse at apex, 4.5–6 by 2.5–4 mm, lilac to purplish, drying blackish, glabrous on both sides. Stamens as long as, or longer than sepals, anthers linear, sometimes tortuose, 1–2 mm long, connectives minutely projected, filaments drying blackish, clavate, glabrous, 3–7 mm long, as broad as, or broader than anther, tapering downwards, rugulose. Achenes 15–80 in a head, fusiform, slightly compressed, 3.5–4.5 by 1.2–1.5 mm, glabrous, 2–4 longitudinally costate on each side, abruptly contracted downwards to shortly stalked, tapering gradually to a hamate beak, 0.8–1.2 mm long.

description: Basal and lower cauline leaves biternate, leaflets broadly obovate or cordate-reniform, 1.2–3 by 1.5–4 cm, cordate to round at base, shallowly 3-lobate, lobes 3–11-crenate-lobulate. Cauline leaves smaller, 1–2-ternate. Achenes 6–21 in a head, drying blackish, fusiform, slightly compressed, 3.5–6 by ca 1.2 mm, shortly stalked.

description: Carnivorous, annual or perennial herbs. Usually hairless. Thai material always small and delicate. Aquatic to terrestrial, always growing in wet places. Leaves diverse in form, often absent at flowering. In terrestrial and semi-aquatic species, the blade, when present, is delicate and few nerved. In aquatic and some semi-aquatic species, the leaves are finely divided into numerous, very thin, linear, hair-like or blood-capillary like segments, which are often microscopically setose and which have no distinct blade. Traps minute, ovoid or globular, present on leaves and / or stolons, capturing and digesting small, often microscopic organisms. Bracts and bracteoles either attached at the base or in the middle. Inflorescence a spike or raceme or, rarely, flowers solitary, occasionally twining (Thai species always twining in a sinistrose or clockwise manner). Flowers hermaphrodite, 5-merous, strongly zygomorphic, sometimes cleistogamous, borne above the surface of the water. Sepals fused, deeply 2-lobed, the lobes more or less free from each other and usually widely divergent. Corolla fused, two-lipped, spurred, with a very short tube: the lower lip often with a conspicuous bump which, in the descriptions which follow, I include as part of the palate. The palate itself lies behind the bump and is often of different colour to the rest of the corolla, may be fringed with hairs and may almost close the mouth of the flower. Stamens 2, inserted on the corolla, filaments short and bent; anthers often connate. Ovary superior, of 2 carpels with a single locule; ovules numerous, on a free-central placenta. Style 1, long, stigma unequally bifid (in some species it has been reported that the lobes of the stigma are either sensitive, closing when touched or after pollination: this, however, has, as far as I know, not yet been observed in Thai material). Fruit usually a vertically circumscissile globose or ovoid capsule. Seeds numerous, minute, almost dust-like in some species, with distinct and varied microscopic surface sculpturing.</br></br>Twenty-seven native species in Thailand. Two additional species which are potentially present, but which are either unrecorded or doubtfully recorded, are also included.</br></br>As is well known, Utricularia catches small prey through its active trapping mechanism. Traps are thin-walled, globose or ovoid and vary in size from ≤ 0.2 mm to usually ≤ 8 mm in Thai species. Untripped traps are flat. When prey passes the entrance to the trap it is sprung, the trap inflates and the prey, together with surrounding water, is sucked into the trap through a hinged trap-door. The door then closes itself in ca 1/500th of a second. The trapped organism dies of anoxia, is digested and the trap eventually resets itself. As well as minute animals it has recently been found that traps may contain algae, and that algae may be present in the absence of trapped animal prey; though whether the algae are actively trapped or merely accidentally sucked in remains to be determined. The trap’s size, morphology and internal structure offer numerous, minute, taxonomic characteristics. Of particular importance are the shape and size of the hairs contained within the trap. These are most easily visualised by cutting open the trap before staining it with Toluidine Blue: the hairs appear as brightly and deeply stained entities which stand out well against the more poorly stained cells of the walls of the trap. Two types of hair are often present in the traps: these bear either two or four arms. The four-armed hairs, sometimes called quadrifids, and in particular the angle, disposition, shape and size of their arms, are of taxonomic value. In some Thai species four-armed hairs are absent altogether and, occasionally, I have found their absence a useful confirmatory characteristic of species identity. The traps are borne in a variety of positions on the plant and what these positions are is also a useful taxonomic characteristic. Finally, the traps are ornamented by appendages which usually occur around the entrance to the trap. The detailed structure of these appendages is taxonomically important. However, because they are extremely fragile, they are often broken or damaged in herbarium material; indeed, in many herbarium specimens they may appear to be entirely absent, but this is an artifact caused by damage. The flowers vary in colour, size and shape and are spurred. The spur also varies, in size, shape and orientation and in the disposition of its internal nectarial glands. Whilst the latter characteristic has been extensively used in the delimitation of certain species in Europe it appears not to have been so far recorded for Thai material.</br></br>The seed-coat is of taxonomic value but its surface features are very difficult to see and, therefore, they have not been extensively used in this account. Unfortunately, the type of hair on the seed’s surface is the only simple morphological means of distinguishing between some of the species of spathulate-leaved Utricularia in Thailand. As the seeds of these species are only 0.2–0.3 mm long and their surface hairs are correspondingly tiny (at an order of magnitude smaller) I have found a pocket microscope of 50 x magnification extremely useful.</br></br>Liquid (50–55% alcohol, 40% water and 5–10% glycerine) preserved material is easier to use than dried herbarium material but unfortunately, collections of liquid preserved material from Thailand are sparse, some of those that exist are not well-maintained and Utricularia’s minute seeds are not easily found again in large volumes of preservative. In general, therefore, it is best to supplement dried with liquid collections rather than relying solely on the latter. The impression that it is almost impossible to correctly identify dried herbarium material is inaccurate - nearly all of it can be identified. Rehydration of dried material is particularly effective in this genus, and I have found that traps from even the most decrepit and elderly specimens can be successfully rehydrated by 36 hours immersion in water at room temperature; the addition of detergent to the water is unnecessary.</br></br>Following Taylor's pragmatic approach I use the term ‘leaves’ rather than 'foliar organs'as used by Maxwell.

description: Suspended aquatic. Stolons filiform, up to 1 m long, occasionally inflated. Rhizoides usually present at the base of the peduncle, branched. Floats rarely present at the base of the peduncle, borne in whorls, ca 2–6 cm long by 3–5 mm wide, the surface with occasional scattered, branched, short filiform rhizoides. Leaves filiform, hair-like, much branched, 2–8 cm long. Auricles (at the base of the leaves) 2–4 mm long, divided into filiform segments, not easily distinguishable from the leaves. Traps usually numerous, ovoid, (1–)4 mm long; mouth lateral, with 2 very fragile appendages (often absent due to damage in dried specimens), often blackish. Internal hairs both 2-armed and 4-armed, the latter or , rarely in shape. Inflorescence erect, emergent, generally solitary, (5–)20(–30) cm long; peduncle hairless, sometimes reddish at base; 5–7-flowered; flowers widely spaced. Scales absent. Bracts ovate, attached at the base, 1–2 mm long, blunt or apiculate at tip, much shorter than pedicels. Bracteoles absent. Pedicels ca 10 mm long and erect in flower; longer, thickened and strongly deflexed in fruit. Calyx lobes ± equal, 2–3 mm long on flowering; up to 9 mm long, enlarging markedly (3 x–5 x) and widely spreading in fruit so that the lobes lie opposite, at 180°, to each other. The maturing fruit lies between the two calyx lobes and almost always is topped by its style; the lobes and fruit form a three pointed star shape when seen in side view. Corolla bright yellow, 1–1.5 cm long; upper lip erect, smaller than lower lip, lower lip downwards facing, with purple guidelines near throat, palate prominent, often deeper yellow and with reddish lines or dots, spur 1–1.5 cm long, subparallel to lower lip, straight or slightly curved, shortly-pointed. Seeds flattened, disc-shaped, usually with 5 sides each with distinct ridged or winged edges, and with a distinct rounded dot like scar in the middle of one of the flat faces, 1–2 mm long.

description: Terrestrial. Stolons numerous, often mat forming, filiform. Rhizoides numerous, filiform, branched. Floats absent. Leaves linear, 0.4–1.5 cm long, 1-nerved (but with 2 very, very faint lateral nerves visible in material with cleared leaves), usually present at flowering. Auricles absent. Traps usually few, mostly on leaves, ca 1–2 mm long; mouth basal, with 2 glandular appendages. Internal hairs unknown. Inflorescence erect, rarely twining, solitary, ca 6–20 cm long; peduncle hairless; usually 2–6-flowered; flowers widely spaced, usually held such that mouth of the flower is horizontal. Scales similar to bracts but 3-nerved. Bracts attached at the base, ovate, ca 2 mm long, acute. Bracteoles setaceous, slightly shorter than the bracts. Pedicels ca 3–5 mm long in flower. Calyx lobes subequal, ca 2–6 mm long on flowering; ovate, the upper acute, the lower sometimes weakly emarginate. Corolla blue or purple; ca 9 mm long, upper lip much smaller than lower lip, the latter conspicuously swollen at the base, palate colour not known; spur ca 3.5–6.5 mm long, usually held parallel to lower lip of calyx, slightly curved. Seeds ovoid, with the testa cells long and narrow and somewhat reticulate; ca 0.3–0.4 mm.

description: Usually terrestrial. Stolons infrequent, filiform. Rhizoides filiform, branched. Floats absent. Leaves linear, usually absent at flowering, 1–2 cm long, 1-nerved. Auricles absent. Traps usually numerous, reniform, 0.5–1 mm long; mouth basal, with 2 very fragile appendages (often absent due to damage in dried specimens), often blackish. Internal hairs 1-armed or 2-armed. Inflorescence erect, solitary, (3–)14(–20) cm long; peduncle hairless; usually 3–7(–15)-flowered; flowers widely spaced, and, when young, often held such that mouth of the flower is upright, the upper lip of the corolla and spur are arranged parallel to the peduncle and that part of the lower lip below the palate is held horizontally. Scales infrequent, similar to bracts. Bracts ovate, attached at the base, 1–1.5 mm long, blunt at tip, occasionally pinkish tinged. Bracteoles subulate, ca 0.5 mm long. Pedicels ca (1–)3–4 mm in flower, and erect; strongly deflexed and enlarged in fruit. Calyx lobes subequal, 2–3 mm long on flowering, the lower sometimes with a shortly bifid/emarginate apex; sometimes reddish tinged, markedly expanded in fruit with the margins forming a conspicuous, flattened rim around the fruit. Corolla usually yellow; 6–10(–12) mm long; very rarely whitish-yellow, upper lip erect, much smaller than lower lip, lower lip spreading horizontally to erect, both occasionally with red markings, palate prominent, often deeper yellow; spur 3–4(–7) mm long, downward facing, straight to slightly curved, long pointed. Seeds ovoid, often with one end clearly truncated, ca 0.5 mm long.

description: Usually terrestrial. Stolons infrequent, filiform. Rhizoides filiform, branched. Floats absent. Leaves rosulate, shortly petiolate, laminar to oblong to spathulate, 2–5 cm long, 3–5-nerved (1-nerved on Ko Kut), present and conspicuous on flowering. Auricles absent. Traps usually few, reniform, 0.5–1 mm long; mouth basal, with 2 very fragile appendages (often absent due to damage in dried specimens). Internal hairs 2-armed (1-armed, not seen). Inflorescence erect, but sometimes straggling and weak, solitary, (8–)15(–30) cm long; peduncle hairless; usually 3–7(–10)-flowered; flowers widely spaced and, when young, often held such that mouth of the flower is upright; the mouth of the flower widely gaping. Scales infrequent, similar to bracts. Bracts ovate, attached at the base, 1.5–2 mm long, acute to acuminate. Bracteoles subulate, ca 0.5 mm long. Pedicels ca 7–15 mm in flower, and erect; deflexed and enlarged in fruit. Calyx lobes unequal, the lower smaller, ca 2.5–3.5 mm long on flowering, sometimes with a shortly bifid / emarginate apex, the upper ca 4 mm on flowering, acute or apiculate; markedly expanded in fruit with the margins forming a conspicuous, flattened rim around the fruit. Corolla yellow; 7–10(–15) mm long; upper lip erect, smaller than lower lip, lower lip spreading horizontally to erect, palate prominent, often deeper yellow; spur 5–6 mm long, downward facing, slightly curved, long-pointed, slightly scented. Seeds ovoid, often with one end clearly truncated; ca 0.5 mm.
